does: Combines a light, airy mixture with a heavier one while keeping as much of the air as possible.

intro.what: Folding brings an airy mixture into a heavier mixture while preserving its volume.
intro.why: It teaches you to lift and turn gently, stopping before repeated mixing knocks the air out.

how: Stir a small part of the whipped mixture into the heavy one to loosen it.
Cut down through the middle with a spatula, sweep along the bottom, and bring it up and over.
Turn the bowl a little and repeat, stopping when only a few streaks remain.

cues.text: An even, light mixture that still stands in soft mounds and has lost little of its volume.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring in circles, which knocks the air out and leaves a flat batter.
mistakes.fix: Cut, lift and turn. Stop early: a few streaks do less harm than more folding.

quiz.question: Why fold rather than stir an airy mixture vigorously?
choices: To retain as much of its air as possible.
To make the foam denser before combining it.
To remove large bubbles through vigorous mixing.
quiz.because: The aim is to combine the mixtures while keeping the volume provided by the air.

quiz.question: What movement combines the mixtures gently?
choices: Stir quickly around the bowl in circles.
Cut down, sweep across the bottom and lift over.
Press the mixtures firmly against the bowl sides.
quiz.because: Cutting, lifting and turning combines the mixture without the flattening effect of circular stirring.

quiz.question: What appearance suggests successful folding?
choices: A flat batter that has lost much of its volume.
Separate heavy lumps beneath untouched foam.
A light mixture that still stands in soft mounds.
quiz.because: Soft mounds and retained volume show the mixture has stayed light as it combined.

quiz.question: Repeated stirring has flattened the batter. What would you change next time?
choices: Use lifting folds and stop before overmixing.
Stir faster until the volume returns.
Continue stirring until every tiny streak disappears.
quiz.because: Overworking knocks air out; a few remaining streaks do less harm than excessive folding.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to fold until something has been whipped.
